science.title: Interfacial hydride transfer for dehalogenation with water
science.description: Reductive dehalogenation of organohalides through hydrodehalogenation with water is critical for environmental and chemical industries. Conventional hydrodehalogenation proceeds via electron transfer pathways (e.g., stepwise electron/hydrogen radical transfer, or two-electron transfer followed by protonation), which are often hampered by limited dehalogenation kinetics and selectivity. While the interfacial transfer of reductive hydride (Hδ−) species presents a compelling concerted two-electron pathway, its application has been constrained by the difficult surface hydride formation under mild conditions. Here, we overcome this challenge by developing mechanochemically activated zero-valent iron (ZVI) that generates reactive silicon-hydride (Si–Hδ⁻) species in the presence of trace water. Trace water induces ZVI corrosion to produce H2, which is heterolytically cleaved by in situ formed surface Siδ+–Oδ⁻ Lewis pairs, yielding nucleophilic Si–Hδ⁻ motifs. These motifs drive direct interfacial hydride transfer for highly efficient hydrodehalogenation and regioselective deuteration with rate constants 2-50 times greater than conventional radical-based hydrogen transfer on ZVI. The water-mediated regeneration of the hydride donor enables continuous-flow decontamination of actual halogenated groundwater and valorization of organohalides into high-purity deuterated products with selectivity of 93.4%. This work presents a promising mechanochemical platform that suggests a more sustainable approach for selective hydrodehalogenation of organohalides. The authors report mechanochemically activated zero-valent iron converts water-generated H2 into surface Si–Hδ⁻ via heterolytic cleavage under mild conditions, enabling efficient hydrodehalogenation reactions.

science.title: Genomic diversity reveals breeding pools in Brazilian tetraploid potato germplasm
science.description: Potato germplasm developed under tropical conditions may contain diversity for breeding, but the Brazilian materials remain poorly characterized. We evaluated 449 tetraploid potato clones, most from Brazilian breeding programs, with 12,595 SNPs. Dosage-aware analyses and STRUCTURE supported four breeding-related clusters. Genetic differentiation between Brazilian and foreign populations was low (ΦST = 0.04), indicating extensive use of external germplasm in Brazilian breeding. In contrast, differentiation among the genetic clusters was moderate (ΦST = 0.22), suggesting preferable restricted parental use in their pipelines. Heterozygosity and inbreeding estimates depended strongly on genotype encoding. Tajima’s D was positive (4.46), and suggested selection favoring increased heterozygosity. Three genome scans identified 92 shared candidate outlier SNPs within broad LD-based windows. The functional annotations generated hypotheses related to stress responses for further studies to be functionally validated. The results provide insights at a panel-level baseline for germplasm management and candidate prioritization in Brazilian potato breeding.
